positive: Many commenters praise the matte, textured inner screen as a clever way to hide the fold crease, with some saying it is barely visible.
The unfolding animation, where the home screen blurs and refocuses as if the front panel were see-through, is widely seen as smooth, clean and inventive.
Several people say the display finish and animation changed their opinion, and that these touches set the phone apart from other foldables.
negative: Many commenters say the crease is still clearly visible and can be felt, so it is reduced but not eliminated.
Several see the matte inner display as a trick to hide the crease, and say it blurs the image and dulls colors.
Some doubt the crease will hold up over time, and question the high price and repair costs given these flaws.

positive: Many Samsung foldable owners say they are impressed by Apple's first foldable, especially the folding animation and overall polish.
Several commenters point out that Samsung has made foldables for years and supplies the screen, so the novelty feels overstated.
Some current Fold users plan to stay with Samsung, and they are enthusiastic about more apps being designed for the format.
negative: Many commenters say Apple is late to foldables and is presenting long-available technology as groundbreaking, often while charging a higher price than Samsung.
The price draws heavy criticism, with commenters saying it is too expensive and joking about the cost.
Some Samsung owners are frustrated that the Fold lacks pen support, flex mode and water resistance, and some say they would pay more for Apple's version.

positive: Many commenters say they are sold on the Duo after seeing it and are eager to buy it once it is released.
Several praise how well the software and hardware work together, and expect Apple's ecosystem to give it an edge over rival foldables.
Some see practical appeal for reading, watching content and travelling with one device, even if the camera isn't the best.
negative: Many commenters would hold off buying until later models, wanting missing features such as Face ID and a telephoto lens, and suspecting Apple is saving them for later.
Price is a major obstacle: the phone is seen as too expensive, especially with extra storage and in local currencies, and a bigger screen doesn't justify it.
Some doubt the foldable's durability, citing a visible crease and the risk of the screen creasing or breaking, and prefer to wait for improvements.

positive: Many commenters praise the fold/unfold animation and overall interface polish, calling it a signature example of Apple's design care.
Several like the display and the minimal crease, and some see the larger screen as a good phone-and-tablet combination.
Some are excited enough to buy it, and they welcome more competition in foldables and developer interest in the form factor.
negative: Many see the price of roughly two thousand dollars as excessive, especially given the economy, and want more storage in the base model.
Commenters say Apple is late to foldables and that fans are praising features Android phones have offered for years.

positive: Viewers like that the larger folding screen could replace carrying an iPad or iPad mini. They mention multitasking, reading, work use and larger text.
Some are happy to upgrade from Pro or Air models, and a few say it beats the Pro lineup. Others would wait for a later Duo version.
negative: Many commenters see the Duo as essentially a small iPad, and say a regular iPhone plus a separate iPad Mini or Pro is cheaper and more sensible.
The price is a major complaint, and many prefer the Pro Max, with its stronger cameras and Face ID, over the Duo's compromises.
Some say a first-generation foldable carries risks, and that Apple is late to a feature Android makers already offer.

positive: Viewers like the side-by-side use of two apps, including scrolling short video feeds together, and see two at a time as a sensible limit.

The smooth transition when unfolding, such as Netflix moving from the cover screen to the open display, impressed people. Netflix adapting its app was seen as evidence of Apple's attention to app experience.
The iPad-like behavior when opened is praised, including volume buttons that suit both portrait and landscape use.
negative: Commenters see the larger-screen app behavior as underwhelming, saying apps mostly look like enlarged versions of the phone layout rather than using the extra space.
Several criticize iOS and the App Store as restrictive, saying it limits foldable features compared with Android alternatives.
Some find the interface tweaks, such as the moved dock and menu buttons overlapping photos, minor or awkward rather than real multitasking gains.

positive: Many commenters prefer an under-display selfie camera because it gives a clean inner screen without a cutout or permanent dot.
Several say the selfie camera is a minor compromise, since they rarely take photos or use the front camera.
Some argue reviewers overstate the camera drawbacks, and that typical buyers would not notice or care about them.
negative: Some commenters want a more capable rear camera setup, such as an extra lens, rather than just two.
Camera bumps are seen as an unwelcome design trend that shouldn't be treated as desirable.
The device is considered too expensive for what it offers, with regional pricing in particular seen as unreasonable compared with simply buying a regular camera.

elements.text: Example of the Slack digest, to show the format. Figures are illustrative and not guaranteed to be accurate. Data through 2026-10-06. Ask a follow-up: mention the app or message it.

examples.q: Which channel sizes break out most, and are their audiences happy? Give n.
examples.a:
Small channels break out most, and their audiences are fairly happy, though mid-size channels have the happiest audiences.

- Small: 37.5% of 56 videos with a baseline outperformed (73 videos total). Net sentiment is +15 (43% positive, 28% negative, n=741 product-side comments).
- Mid: 15.6% of 32 videos outperformed. Net sentiment is +22 (48% positive, 25% negative, n=416).
- Large: 12.5% of 24 videos with a baseline outperformed (31 total). Net sentiment is +1 (38% positive, 37% negative, n=384), so opinion is split.

The small group's average lift of 6.7x is probably pulled up by a few big hits. Mid and large groups have modest sample sizes, and these are associations in a comment sample, not causes.
examples.sql:
WITH v AS (
  SELECT c.video_id,
    CASE WHEN cr.tier IN ('nano <50k','micro 50-250k') THEN 'small'
         WHEN cr.tier='mid 250k-1M' THEN 'mid'
         WHEN cr.tier IN ('macro 1-5M','mega 5M+') THEN 'large' END AS size_group,
    p.outperformer, p.rel_lift
  FROM content c
  JOIN creators cr ON cr.channel_id=c.channel_id
  LEFT JOIN performance p ON p.video_id=c.video_id
  WHERE c.topic='duo' AND c.format!='official'
),
perf AS (
  SELECT size_group, COUNT(*) AS n_videos, COUNT(outperformer) AS n_with_baseline,
    ROUND(AVG(outperformer),3) AS outperformer_rate,
    ROUND(AVG(rel_lift),3) AS avg_rel_lift
  FROM v GROUP BY size_group
),
sent AS (
  SELECT v.size_group, COUNT(*) AS n_product_side,
    ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN m.sentiment='positive' THEN 1.0 ELSE 0 END),3) AS pct_positive,
    ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN m.sentiment='negative' THEN 1.0 ELSE 0 END),3) AS pct_negative,
    ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN m.sentiment='positive' THEN 1.0 ELSE 0 END)-AVG(CASE WHEN m.sentiment='negative' THEN 1.0 ELSE 0 END),3) AS net_sentiment
  FROM comments m JOIN v ON v.video_id=m.video_id
  WHERE m.lang='en' AND m.trivial=0 AND m.target IN ('product','price_value','apple_brand','competitor')
  GROUP BY v.size_group
)
SELECT p.size_group, p.n_videos, p.n_with_baseline, p.outperformer_rate, p.avg_rel_lift,
  s.n_product_side, s.pct_positive, s.pct_negative,
  CASE WHEN s.n_product_side>=10 THEN s.net_sentiment END AS net_sentiment
FROM perf p LEFT JOIN sent s ON s.size_group=p.size_group
ORDER BY p.outperformer_rate DESC
LIMIT 40

examples.q: Which content formats work best for mid-sized channels?
examples.a:
First impressions work best for mid-sized channels. Across 13 videos, 30.8% outperformed their baseline, average relative lift was 1.68, and net sentiment was +26 (n=160 product-side comments).

Explainer/tips is a distant second: 6 videos, 16.7% outperformers, lift 1.12, net sentiment +15 (n=88).

No outperformers appeared in the other formats:
- Comparison: 3 videos, lift 0.97, net sentiment +6 (n=35).
- Upgrade advice: 6 videos, lift 0.36, net sentiment +30 (n=37). Viewers like it, but the videos underperform on views.
- Other: 3 videos, lift 0.56, net sentiment +41 (n=29).
- Keynote recap: 1 video, net sentiment -45 (n=11). That is far too small to read anything into.

Caveat: apart from first impressions, the video counts are small, and these are associations, not proof that the format caused the results.
examples.sql: SELECT format, COUNT(*) AS n_videos, SUM(CASE WHEN outperformer IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS n_with_baseline, ROUND(AVG(outperformer),3) AS outperformer_rate, ROUND(AVG(rel_lift),3) AS avg_rel_lift, SUM(CASE WHEN n_product_side>=10 THEN n_product_side ELSE 0 END) AS n_product_side_comments, ROUND(1.0*SUM(CASE WHEN n_product_side>=10 THEN (pct_positive-pct_negative)*n_product_side ELSE 0 END)/NULLIF(SUM(CASE WHEN n_product_side>=10 THEN n_product_side ELSE 0 END),0),3) AS net_sentiment FROM v_content WHERE topic='duo' AND format!='official' AND tier='mid 250k-1M' GROUP BY format ORDER BY outperformer_rate DESC, avg_rel_lift DESC LIMIT 40

examples.q: Which high-lift videos have the most negative audience reaction? Name two examples, with lift and sentiment shown separately.
examples.a:
The two high-lift videos with the most negative reaction are:

1. Melodie Perez's "THE IPHONE DUO IS MADE FOR CONTENT CREATORS" short. Net sentiment is -57 (14% positive, 71% negative, n=14). Lift is 591.7 (rel_lift 58.3) on about 1.56M views.

2. Man of Many's "Apple iPhone Duo Crease Test". Net sentiment is -50 (12.5% positive, 62.5% negative, n=16). Lift is 128.8 (rel_lift 12.7) on about 279K views.

UrAvgConsumer's crease video is close behind at -47 (n=19).

Lift measures reach and sentiment measures tone, so they are separate. Both samples are small (n=14 and n=16), so a few comments could shift the scores. These are also comment samples, and the link between lift and tone is an association, not a cause.
examples.sql: WITH s AS (SELECT video_id, COUNT(*) AS n_product_side, SUM(sentiment='positive') AS pos, SUM(sentiment='negative') AS neg FROM comments WHERE lang='en' AND trivial=0 AND target IN ('product','price_value','apple_brand','competitor') GROUP BY video_id) SELECT c.video_id, c.title, cr.name AS creator, c.format, p.views, ROUND(p.lift,3) AS lift, ROUND(p.rel_lift,3) AS rel_lift, p.outperformer, s.n_product_side, ROUND(1.0*s.pos/s.n_product_side,3) AS pct_positive, ROUND(1.0*s.neg/s.n_product_side,3) AS pct_negative, ROUND(1.0*(s.pos-s.neg)/s.n_product_side,3) AS net_sentiment FROM content c JOIN creators cr ON cr.channel_id=c.channel_id JOIN performance p ON p.video_id=c.video_id JOIN s ON s.video_id=c.video_id WHERE c.topic='duo' AND c.format!='official' AND p.outperformer=1 AND s.n_product_side>=10 ORDER BY net_sentiment ASC, p.rel_lift DESC LIMIT 10

examples.q: Which audience topics are largest, and which are growing fastest this week?
examples.a:
Review praise and feedback is the largest topic (n=310, 14.1% of comments), followed by Duo versus other iPhones (n=268, 12.2%) and Apple's foldable and pricing (n=231, 10.5%). Samsung Fold comparison and Plans to buy the Duo are tied at n=204 each (9.3%).

Samsung Fold comparison is growing fastest: 25 comments the prior week to 103 this week (+312%), and its share of all comments rose 3.9 points. Apple's foldable and pricing (39 to 109, +180%) and Crease and matte screen (15 to 42, +180%) come next, then Plans to buy (+176%) and Duo versus other iPhones (+149%).

Review praise nearly doubled (+98%) but lost 3.5 points of share, so it is growing more slowly than the product topics.

Multitasking and app support went from 8 to 30, but the prior-week n is small, so its growth rate was not calculated. These counts come from a comment sample.
examples.sql: WITH base AS (SELECT c.topic_id, c.day_since_launch AS d FROM comments c JOIN content v ON v.video_id=c.video_id WHERE v.topic='duo' AND v.format!='official' AND c.lang='en' AND c.trivial=0), mx AS (SELECT MAX(d) AS m FROM base), tot AS (SELECT COUNT(*) AS n_all, SUM(CASE WHEN d>(SELECT m FROM mx)-7 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS wk_all, SUM(CASE WHEN d<=(SELECT m FROM mx)-7 AND d>(SELECT m FROM mx)-14 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS pr_all FROM base), t AS (SELECT topic_id, COUNT(*) AS n_total, SUM(CASE WHEN d>(SELECT m FROM mx)-7 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS n_this_week, SUM(CASE WHEN d<=(SELECT m FROM mx)-7 AND d>(SELECT m FROM mx)-14 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS n_prior_week FROM base WHERE topic_id IS NOT NULL GROUP BY topic_id) SELECT tp.topic_id, tp.name, tp.pool, tp.origin, tp.first_seen, t.n_total, ROUND(t.n_total*1.0/tot.n_all,3) AS share_of_all, t.n_this_week, t.n_prior_week, t.n_this_week-t.n_prior_week AS wow_change, CASE WHEN t.n_prior_week>=10 THEN ROUND((t.n_this_week-t.n_prior_week)*1.0/t.n_prior_week,3) END AS wow_growth_pct, ROUND(t.n_this_week*1.0/NULLIF(tot.wk_all,0)-t.n_prior_week*1.0/NULLIF(tot.pr_all,0),3) AS share_shift, (SELECT m FROM mx) AS latest_day FROM t JOIN topics tp ON tp.topic_id=t.topic_id CROSS JOIN tot ORDER BY t.n_total DESC LIMIT 40

examples.q: How does audience sentiment on the main product compare with the other products in the data?
examples.a:
Duo sentiment is mildly positive at +17 net (n=1,392 comments across 129 videos), with 44% positive, 28% neutral and 27% negative.

The other topics have far fewer comments, so the comparisons are rough:
- Event general: +2 net (n=55, 6 videos), so it is more mixed than Duo. Positive is 33% and negative is 31%.
- Other: +25 net (n=28, 4 videos), slightly above Duo, but the sample is small.
- Competitor foldable: -45 net (n=11, 1 video). Only 9% are positive and 55% negative. This is one video and very small.
- iPhone 18 Pro: n=4, too few to score, so no net sentiment is reported.

Only Duo has a sample large enough to trust. These figures come from a comment sample, so treat the other topics as directional at best.
examples.sql: SELECT c.topic, COUNT(*) AS n_product_side, COUNT(DISTINCT cm.video_id) AS n_videos, ROUND(AVG(cm.sentiment='positive'),3) AS pct_positive, ROUND(AVG(cm.sentiment='neutral'),3) AS pct_neutral, ROUND(AVG(cm.sentiment='negative'),3) AS pct_negative, CASE WHEN COUNT(*)>=10 THEN ROUND(AVG(cm.sentiment='positive')-AVG(cm.sentiment='negative'),3) END AS net_sentiment FROM comments cm JOIN content c ON c.video_id=cm.video_id WHERE cm.lang='en' AND cm.trivial=0 AND cm.target IN ('product','price_value','competitor') AND c.format!='official' GROUP BY c.topic ORDER BY (c.topic='duo') DESC, n_product_side DESC LIMIT 40

examples.q: What do people like most about iPhone Duo, and what do they criticise most?
examples.a:
Commenters like the Duo most when they talk about buying it and about the crease and matte screen. Criticism is milder and centres on pricing and comparisons.

Most liked:
- Plans to buy: net +35 (51% positive, 16% negative, n=186).
- Crease and matte screen: net +26 (50% positive, 24% negative, n=169).
- Under-display camera and lenses scores +37, but n=27 is small, so treat it cautiously.

Most criticised, by negative share:
- Apple's foldable and pricing: net +14 (46% positive, 32% negative, n=182).
- Samsung Fold comparison: net +9 (41% positive, 32% negative, n=99).
- Duo versus other iPhones: net +11 (41% positive, 30% negative, n=240).

No topic is net negative, so "criticised" here means the most mixed topics. These figures come from a sample of English comments on non-official videos.
examples.sql: WITH base AS (SELECT t.name AS topic_name, c.sentiment FROM comments c JOIN content v ON v.video_id=c.video_id JOIN topics t ON t.topic_id=c.topic_id WHERE c.lang='en' AND c.trivial=0 AND v.topic='duo' AND v.format!='official' AND c.target IN ('product','price_value') AND t.pool='product'), agg AS (SELECT topic_name, COUNT(*) AS n, SUM(sentiment='positive') AS n_pos, SUM(sentiment='negative') AS n_neg FROM base GROUP BY topic_name) SELECT * FROM (SELECT 'liked' AS side, topic_name, n, n_pos, n_neg, ROUND(1.0*n_pos/n,3) AS pos_share, ROUND(1.0*n_neg/n,3) AS neg_share FROM agg ORDER BY n_pos DESC LIMIT 8) UNION ALL SELECT * FROM (SELECT 'criticised' AS side, topic_name, n, n_pos, n_neg, ROUND(1.0*n_pos/n,3) AS pos_share, ROUND(1.0*n_neg/n,3) AS neg_share FROM agg ORDER BY n_neg DESC LIMIT 8)
